questions.question: According to the debugging guide, what should be your first stop when an MCP integration misbehaves?

options.text: Rewriting the server in another language
The MCP Inspector — an interactive, transport-agnostic testing UI
Filing a GitHub issue immediately
Packet capture with Wireshark

questions.explanation: The Inspector lets you connect to stdio or Streamable HTTP servers, invoke tools/prompts/resources, and watch the notification stream — it should be your first stop before deeper debugging.

questions.question: Where does Claude Desktop write its MCP-related log files on macOS?

options.text: /var/log/claude/
~/Library/Logs/Claude (e.g., mcp.log and mcp-server-SERVERNAME.log)
~/Documents/Claude/logs
/tmp/claude-mcp.log

questions.explanation: Logs live in ~/Library/Logs/Claude: mcp.log contains general connection logging, and mcp-server-SERVERNAME.log files capture each server's stderr output. On Windows they're under %APPDATA%\Claude\logs.

questions.question: For a server using the Streamable HTTP transport, how should you handle logging (as opposed to a stdio server)?

options.text: stderr is captured by the client, so keep using it
Use server-side log aggregation or OpenTelemetry, plus standard HTTP tooling to inspect requests — the client does not capture stderr
Send everything via notifications/message, the recommended mechanism
HTTP servers cannot log at all

questions.explanation: For stdio servers, stderr is captured by the host automatically. For Streamable HTTP servers the client doesn't capture stderr, so use your own aggregation or OpenTelemetry; note that protocol-level logging (notifications/message) is deprecated as of 2026-07-28.

questions.question: A request is rejected with error code -32021 (MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError). What does this indicate?

options.text: The server does not support the requested protocol version
The server needs a capability (such as elicitation) that the request's clientCapabilities in _meta did not declare
The tool arguments failed schema validation
The OAuth token expired

questions.explanation: -32021 names client capabilities the server requires but the request didn't declare. By contrast, -32022 (UnsupportedProtocolVersionError) lists the server's supported versions, and -32602 (Invalid params) covers requests missing required _meta fields or otherwise malformed input.

questions.question: MCP servers launched over stdio inherit only a limited set of environment variables. How do you provide additional ones in claude_desktop_config.json?

options.text: They must be baked into the binary
Add an env key to the server's entry, e.g., "env": { "MYAPP_API_KEY": "some_key" }
Set them in the shell before launching Claude; they always propagate
Use a .envrc file next to the config

questions.explanation: Stdio-launched servers inherit only a limited, platform-dependent subset of environment variables, so custom variables are specified via the env key in the server's configuration entry.

questions.question: How do clients opt in to receiving log messages from a server under the 2026-07-28 per-request logging model?

options.text: By calling logging/setLevel once per session
By setting the io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel field in the request's _meta; servers must not send notifications/message for requests that omit it
Logging is always on at debug level
By subscribing to a logs:// resource

questions.explanation: MCP defines eight RFC 5424 severity levels, and clients opt in per request via the io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel _meta field. This replaces the legacy session-wide logging/setLevel model (and the mechanism as a whole is deprecated in favor of stderr/OpenTelemetry).

questions.question: How do you enable Chrome DevTools inside Claude Desktop for client-side debugging?

options.text: It is enabled by default with F12
Create a developer_settings.json containing {"allowDevTools": true}, then open DevTools with Command-Option-I (macOS) or Ctrl+Alt+I (Windows)
Launch Claude with the --devtools flag
Install a separate debug build of Claude

questions.explanation: Writing {"allowDevTools": true} to developer_settings.json in Claude's application support directory enables DevTools; you'll see two windows (main content and title bar) and can use the Console and Network panels to inspect errors, payloads, and timing.

questions.question: For a local stdio server, what happens to messages the server writes to stderr?

options.text: They are discarded
They are captured automatically by the host application (e.g., into Claude Desktop's mcp-server-NAME.log)
They corrupt the protocol like stdout does
They are sent to the model as context

questions.explanation: With the stdio transport, everything logged to stderr is captured by the host automatically — which is why stderr is the correct logging destination for stdio servers, while stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC.

questions.question: Which events does the debugging guide list as important to log?

options.text: Startup steps, resource access, tool execution, error conditions, and performance metrics
Only fatal crashes
User passwords for reproduction
Nothing; logging slows servers down

questions.explanation: Important events to log: startup steps, resource access, tool execution, error conditions, and performance metrics — with structured formats, context, timestamps, and request IDs.

questions.question: Where are Claude Desktop's MCP log files located on Windows?

options.text: C:\Program Files\Claude\logs
%APPDATA%\Claude\logs
C:\Windows\Temp\claude
The Windows Event Viewer only

questions.explanation: On Windows the logs are under %APPDATA%\Claude\logs (on macOS: ~/Library/Logs/Claude). They capture connection events, configuration issues, runtime errors, and message exchanges.

questions.question: How many log severity levels does MCP define, and from which standard do they come?

options.text: Three levels from POSIX
Eight levels (debug through emergency) from RFC 5424 (syslog)
Five levels from log4j
Ten custom levels

questions.explanation: MCP defines eight RFC 5424 severity levels, from debug through emergency. Under 2026-07-28, clients opt in per request via the io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel _meta field.

questions.question: SCENARIO: Your server runs perfectly when you launch it from your project directory in a terminal, but fails to find its data files when Claude Desktop launches it. What's the most likely cause?

options.text: Claude Desktop blocks file access entirely
The server uses relative paths, and the working directory of a client-launched server may be undefined (like / on macOS) — switch to absolute paths in config and .env files
The transport changed from stdio to HTTP
Node and Python resolve paths differently

questions.explanation: Servers launched via a client's config can't rely on the working directory. Testing from a terminal masks the problem because the cwd is your project directory. The fix is absolute paths everywhere; the env key may also be needed since stdio servers inherit a limited environment.

questions.question: SCENARIO: A hand-rolled client's requests are all rejected with error -32602 (Invalid params), even simple tools/list calls. Given the 2026-07-28 per-request metadata rules, what should you check first?

options.text: Whether the server is out of disk space
Whether every request's _meta carries the required io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities fields — a request missing either is rejected with -32602
Whether the JSON-RPC id is a UUID
Whether OAuth scopes include mcp:tools

questions.explanation: Every request must carry protocolVersion and clientCapabilities in _meta (and should carry clientInfo). Requests missing a required field are rejected with -32602 — the same code as other malformed input — so inspecting _meta is the first debugging step.

questions.question: SCENARIO: A client fails to connect to a server and you suspect a protocol-version mismatch. Per the debugging guide, how do you confirm and resolve it?

options.text: Downgrade the client until it works
Call server/discover to see the server's supported versions; if you get UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022), its data field lists the versions the server supports, so you can pick a mutual one
Clear the DNS cache
Increase the connection timeout

questions.explanation: The connection-problems checklist says to verify protocol compatibility by calling server/discover; a -32022 error explicitly lists the server's supported versions in its data field, telling you exactly which version to retry with.

questions.question: According to the 'testing changes' guidance, which tool supports the quickest iteration loop while developing a server?

options.text: Rebuilding the host application
The MCP Inspector — while configuration or server-code changes in a client like Claude Desktop require a full client restart
Editing the model's system prompt
tcpdump

questions.explanation: For quick iteration, use the Inspector during development. Configuration and server code changes in a real client require restarting it (fully quitting Claude Desktop, not just closing the window).

questions.question: A server launched through stdio immediately disconnects. Which debugging sequence is most aligned with the study guide?

options.text: Change OAuth scopes, then clear DNS, then retrain the model
Check client logs, verify the server process, test it standalone in Inspector, then check version/capability compatibility
Delete all tools and retry
Switch to legacy HTTP+SSE first

questions.explanation: The guide's connection-failure checklist starts with logs/process state, then standalone Inspector testing, then server/discover/version-capability checks.

questions.question: A server works in Inspector but not in the desktop host. What does that evidence most strongly suggest?

options.text: The MCP server can never be at fault
Focus next on host-specific launch configuration, environment, permissions, or compatibility rather than assuming basic server functionality is broken
Inspector guarantees production security
The server must use port 6274

questions.explanation: Passing standalone Inspector tests narrows the fault domain. It does not prove perfection, but it makes host-specific configuration/environment a high-value next area to investigate.

questions.question: A tester sees readable log lines mixed into a captured stdio protocol transcript. What is the most diagnostic next check?

options.text: Whether the server is writing logs to stdout instead of stderr
Whether the OAuth audience is plural
Whether tasks/get is enabled
Whether the Registry name uses reverse DNS

questions.explanation: Readable logs in the protocol stream strongly suggest stdout contamination. For stdio, logs belong on stderr.
